name: Chore Rewards
tagline: Android app for assigning household chores to kids and paying them out in points or pocket money.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a to-do list with a points ledger and a family of users, which is roughly the canonical CRUD app. There is no proprietary data, no network of other families making the app better, and no integration that matters: the chores are whatever you type in, and the rewards are settled by a parent handing over cash or screen time. An agent can produce a working self-hosted version with profiles, recurring chores, approval flow, and a running balance in a single sitting. The honest catch is delivery: you get a web app on your home network or a small VPS, not something a nine year old taps on the home screen after an app store install. If your household can live with a PWA shortcut and no push notifications, the paid version stops being necessary almost immediately.
coreLoopDIY: Parents create recurring chores and assign them to kid profiles, kids mark them done, parents approve, and points accrue into a balance that can be spent on a rewards list.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine that stays on: old laptop, Raspberry Pi, or a cheap VPS
Phones on the same wifi, or Tailscale if you want it to work outside the house
Someone willing to be the admin who approves completed chores
whatYouLose: A real installable Android app with an icon, versus a bookmarked web page
Push notifications and daily reminders, which is a lot of what makes chore apps actually work on kids
Hosted sync and backups: your data lives on whatever box you left running
Kid-friendly polish: animations, sounds, avatars, the small dopamine stuff that is the entire product for a seven year old
Any built-in reward redemption, gift cards or bank transfers, if the paid app offers that
moatNotes: The moat here is not technical, it is that the kids already know the app and re-teaching a family a new system is genuine work.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a few dollars is less than an evening of your life, and because a chore app only functions if the children actually open it. A native app with a home screen icon and nagging notifications beats a superior self-hosted web app that nobody remembers to load. Parents are also not usually shopping for a system they will have to maintain: the whole point of the purchase is offloading household administration, not adding a server to it.
notes: The build is easy; getting your children to use it is the part no agent can one-shot.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted family chore and rewards tracker that runs on a home network.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/chores.db, schema created on boot
- No auth provider, no cloud services, no analytics, no telemetry

Data model:
- household members: name, role (parent or kid), avatar emoji, 4 digit PIN
- chores: title, notes, points, assigned member, schedule (once, daily, weekly on chosen weekdays)
- chore instances: generated for the current and next 7 days, status of open, submitted, approved, or skipped
- rewards: title, cost in points, optional stock count
- ledger: append only rows of points earned or spent, with reason and timestamp

Behavior:
- Landing page is a profile picker showing every member as a large tap target
- Kid view: today and this week's chores, one tap to mark submitted, a points balance, and a rewards list where they can request a redemption
- Parent view (PIN gated): approve or reject submitted chores, create and edit chores and rewards, adjust points manually with a required reason, see per kid history
- Approving a chore writes a ledger row; redeeming a reward writes a negative one; balance is always computed from the ledger, never stored
- Recurring chore instances are generated lazily on page load, idempotent by chore id plus date

UI:
- Mobile first, big buttons, high contrast, readable by a child
- Include a web app manifest and icons so it can be added to a phone home screen
- No animations beyond a simple confirmation state

Explicitly out of scope: push notifications, email, real money payouts, multi household support, any external API.

Deliver a README with setup, how to run it on the local network with a fixed port, and a one command SQLite backup. Any config goes in .env.example, never hardcoded.
